root_cause.text: `pipapo_drop()` in `net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c` unconditionally reads `rulemap[i + 1].n` from a stack-allocated `rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS]` array even on the last field iteration, causing an out-of-bounds stack read before `pipapo_unmap()` can return early.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `bool last = i == m->field_count - 1;` and changes the call from `rulemap[i + 1].n` to `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n`, while the CVE description states that the last iteration (`i == m->field_count - 1`) accessed one element past the end of `rulemap` and KASAN reported a stack-out-of-bounds read at exactly 4 bytes past the array.

vuln_statements.content: pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n, rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1);

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a per-field `last` flag to distinguish the final pipapo field during drop processing.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable `last` is declared inside the `nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m)` loop and initialized to `i == m->field_count - 1` before the inner `for (g = 0; g < f->groups; g++)` loop.
intent_record.how: This change makes the code aware of whether the current field is the final field in the match structure, likely so later logic in the function can treat the last field differently at runtime. By itself in this hunk, it only introduces the per-iteration state needed for such conditional handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pipapo unmapping to avoid using the next field index on the last field by passing 0 when `last` is true.
intent_record.what: In the call to pipapo_unmap(), the fifth argument was changed from `rulemap[i + 1].n` to `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n`, and the sixth argument remains the `last` flag.
intent_record.how: When processing the last field, the code now passes 0 instead of reading the next rulemap entry, avoiding use of an out-of-range/irrelevant value for the final unmap operation while preserving the existing behavior for non-final fields.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this snippet. In `pipapo_drop()`, the code iterates over all fields with `nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m)` and then unconditionally calls `pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n, rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1);`. Because `rulemap` is declared as `union nft_pipapo_map_bucket rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS];`, the access to `rulemap[i + 1].n` on the last field is an out-of-bounds read from the stack array, exactly matching the root cause. There is no guard or special-case here to avoid reading `rulemap[i + 1]` for the last iteration, so the fix is not present.
